notebooks.title: Challenging Determinism in Value Formation
notebooks.summary: Evaluates the feasibility of assuming deterministic outcomes in WAKE's provider-based architecture and identifies potential measurement artifacts.

notebooks.next_questions: Is the observed divergence a result of platform-level non-determinism or a flaw in the testing harness?

notebooks.title: Memories and Reference Frames in Preference Formation
notebooks.summary: A synthesized investigation into how map-like computations and hierarchical data structures enable preference formation, alongside the role of architectural boundaries in shaping artificial 'preferences' or system-level behaviors.
notebooks.findings:
Preference formation relies on reference frame transformations supported by hierarchical data structures. [source-177acf3afcad4269] [source-cab212cbfcaa4873]

System-level interactions are bounded by strict information partitions, influencing how experiences are accumulated. [source-a1a50071f9ec48e7]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence from behavioral neuroscience (hippocampal reference frames) and abstract perception models is distinct from the functional constraints of the WAKE provider architecture. The leap from biological/algorithmic preference formation to artificial system-level agency remains speculative and lacks a unified computational framework.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the 'provider boundary' mechanism—which strictly separates state from computation—function as a limiting factor in emergent preference formation? Can we experimentally demonstrate 'anchoring-and-adjustment' biases in WAKE's interaction patterns?
notebooks.reason: This revision incorporates architectural constraints from the WAKE provider boundary as a structural analogy for how systems partition memory and experience, fulfilling the requirement for new evidence integration in the notebook revision process.
